sentences: The divorcee (an actress) returns to her coastal-city home following a divorce to see her boyfriend the gentleman (an actor).
They visit nightclub the nightspot, where the gentleman tells the divorcee that he has fallen in love with another woman.
Saddened, the divorcee tries to kill herself, but a bystander (an actor) prevents her from doing so.

Meanwhile, the young man (an actor) has discovered that the suspect (an actor), who murdered club performer the entertainer, has been released as the police believe there is not enough evidence that the suspect killed her.
Although the young man witnessed the killing, he is afraid to see police, fearing that the suspect will go after his girlfriend the young lady (an actress).
The young man instead decides to phone the police, but the operator (an actress) listens in on the phone call and informs the suspect of the young man's actions.
The suspect hires a gunman to murder the young man, but the killer shoots the operator after she shouts a warning to the young man, and she ends up hitting the gunman with her car.
As the young man goes to the police station to testify, the gentleman and the divorcee decide to get back together and go home.
The painter is a returning World War II veteran That visit the doctor's office to explain his concern about lapses in his memory.
The doctor, a psychiatrist, explains to the painter that he may be experiencing 'transient amnesia'.
The condition is characterized by headaches and no memory of the events.
While painting a model, he begins to experience severe headaches.
He calls the doctor to tell him he believes he's going to have another episode and to come to his studio apartment immediately.
The painter explains to the model that he is going to go out to the roof to get some air and to clear his head.
In the next scene we see someone sneaking into the apartment and attacks the model.
The murderer dropped the key under the sofa.
During a party in the painter's apartment his beautiful girlfriend is found dead under a sofa, murdered.
The police suspect the painter of the killing, but the crime-solving psychiatrist is not so sure, and proceeds to investigate further.

The detective, a supremely intelligent police detective, must solve a series of brutal murders in which the victims, all from different social and economic backgrounds, are viciously slashed to pieces by the one known as the scarred killer.
Suspects abound but the detective must find the common link of extortion and revenge before more are killed.

The detective narrowly misses the scarred killer at the scene of his second murder, but does encounter a rooftop astronomer, the professor, and it seems unlikely that the scarred killer went unseen by him.
Arrested on suspicion, his "mystic" attitude confounds police interrogators.
A knife left behind at a murder scene is traced to the home/business of mortician the undertaker.
The layout of his business suggests it would be easy to steal from his supply room.
The detective leaves to pursue leads at the local nightclub, taking the girlfriend along as "cover".
But when the undertaker doesn't answer his phone all evening, the detective returns there and finds him murdered.
The city's mayor has been receiving death threats, even though he is "well above" the other victims in status.
The mayor finally remembers, at the detective's prodding, that he served as a juror before he went into politics.
A hulking man named the knifeman was found guilty of knifing his sweetheart to death.
The detective puts out an APB on the knifeman.
The professor has been released on a writ.
It develops that he is the scarred killer's silent partner, but had written extortion notes on his own; hoping to make money on the side.
The scarred killer considers this a breach of trust and brutally murders the professor, tossing him through a skylight.
The scarred killer boldly goes to the detective's rooming house and kidnaps the girlfriend as "leverage".
The detective's young ward tails the getaway car and leaves a trail for the police.
The detective conquers the scarred killer in a brutal fistfight and life at the precinct returns to normal (with the girlfriend once again stood up for a dinner date by a homicide).
During the final months of World War II, a young man is hitchhiking to the small town.
After several failed attempts, he finally steps in front of a car driven by a young woman.
She tries to go around him, but crashes and blows out a tire.
He changes the tire in exchange for a ride from the hostile woman.

In addition to blaming him for causing her accident, she resents that he has somehow avoided military service, but when he goes to get some gas, she discovers a uniform (with many decorations) in his suitcase and becomes friendlier to him.
They reveal their odd names, but nothing else about themselves: he is the young man and she is "the young woman".

He is sure that she is a spoiled rich girl, and in fact the young woman is indeed a member of a wealthy high-society family, running from an arranged marriage to another socially prominent type, stolid the fiancé.
Acting on the reported theft of the fiancé's car, the police stop the pair and put them in jail.
After the police talk to the fiancé on the telephone, the two are released.
The young woman takes the young man to the family mansion, telling him that she is the family's secretary.
Having lost her key, she has him crawl through a window, causing the pair to be taken into custody again.
Her identity is finally established, but reporters at the police station get a hold of the story.
The pair are again released.

The young woman initially thinks that the young man is an Army deserter, but after he explains he received a medical discharge, she gives him a job as the family chauffeur, though the old servant, the eccentric old caretaker of the estate, has misgivings.

The young woman's widowed mother, the matriarch, "old maid" the aunt, and younger sister the younger girl all return from the big city, along with the fiancé and his physical trainer and sidekick, the strongman.
The matriarch and the fiancé strongly disapprove of the young woman's association with a presumed gold digger.
The matriarch tries to buy the young man off, while the fiancé sends the strongman to get the police.
The young man, however, is determined to win the young woman's heart.
After a series of family arguments and complications, the young man is revealed to be a nationally known war hero.
He was hitchhiking simply because he does not like publicity.
He is warmly welcomed by the mayor and the governor, and honored with a parade by the town.
His killed-in-battle friend described his hometown so vividly to the young man and later bequeathed it to him, so, having no real ties to any other place, he decided to settle there.
As the young man is being driven away, the young woman sets out after him in her wedding dress, and in a role reversal, he gives her a ride.
The publisher of the first newspaper, the newspaperman, who is used to ordering his staff around, finds that he is ignored by everyone in his own home.
He is shocked when he discovers a scandalous picture of his own daughter, the young woman, on the front page of the competing paper, the rival newspaper.
The newspaperman pays a visit to the dubious publisher of the competing paper, the rival, and warns him not to ever publish a picture like that again, or the newspaperman will kill him.
The newspaperman is unaware of the fact that a man named the crook has overheard his conversation with the rival, which the crook later reveals to him, threatening to expose him.
The newspaperman counters by claiming that the rival was the one who got the crook sentenced with his testimony, and that the rival dated the crook's girlfriend while he was in prison.
To avoid further complications, the newspaperman takes a long vacation, following the suggestion of his chauffeur.
While the newspaperman is away, without his family, the crook murders publisher the rival and hides the body in the trunk of the newspaperman's parked roadster car.

The crook also breaks into the rival's safe, trying to get back a written confession of a previous murder, but finds out the document is missing from the safe and must have been hidden on the publisher the rival's body.
The newspaperman has brought his car on the vacation and finds the rival's dead body in the trunk when he arrives at his hunting lodge.
Panicking, he decides to dump the body to not be accused of murder, but his chauffeur sees the body before he has a chance to carry out his plan.
The chauffeur, eager to protect his employer, removes the body from the car's trunk and hides it inside the lodge.
Visitors come and go at the lodge during the vacation, and the body is moved and hidden several times by the two men to avoid discovery.
Soon enough, the crook also comes looking for the body to retrieve the document.
When the newspaperman's family one day discovers that he has left on vacation, they also come up to the lodge to visit.
Other family members also arrive at the lodge, and even a news reporter from the rival newspaper, trying to get another scandalous story to publish in the paper, shows up as well.
The body is discovered by every visitor at the lodge at some point, and the chauffeur has to move it constantly to confuse the guests.
The newspaperman convinces them all that they have hallucinated.
The local police officer, the constable, discovers the rival's car hidden not far from the cabin, left there by the crook.
The constable immediately suspects the newspaperman of murdering the rival and arrests him.

The young man, the newspaperman's son, falsely claims to have murdered the rival to protect the newspaperman from arrest, but then the rival's body is found, with the confession in one of his pockets.
The crook is arrested for the rival's murder and the murder related to the confession.
The crook admits his guilt when he learns that the constable has the confession, and the newspaperman is cleared of all suspicion.
After the commotion, the newspaperman's family promises to not ignore him anymore.
Despite this, the newspaperman finds himself sitting alone at breakfast the next day.
The pollster (an actor), who works for the polling company ("like the famous poll, but not as fast"), is sent out to find a missing co-worker, the missing man.
He goes to see the last family the man was supposed to interview, the nutty and murderous family.
There he runs afoul of the first twin and the second twin (both played by another actor), the gun-toting twin sons of the mother (an actress).

As matriarch of the clan the mother insists that the pollster, to escape death at the hands of the first twin or the second twin, pretend to be the boyfriend of the jailed robber in order to gain the confidence of her dying grandmother (a second actress).

The grandmother has hidden $70,000 stolen by the robber and her now-executed father, but refuses to divulge where to her unwanted relations for a very good reason: she tells the pollster that she has been poisoned by them.
Before she dies, she teaches the pollster a nonsensical song which is also known to the girl (a third actress), the mother's dimwitted daughter.
The family are sure the grandmother told the pollster where the money is hidden and keep him captive.
Then, a woman claiming to be the robber shows up, also looking for the loot.
When she gets the pollster alone for questioning, she reveals she is actually the young woman (a fourth actress).
Her innocent father was maliciously implicated by the robber's father in the bank robbery.
The pollster wants to escape, now that they are alone, but the young woman insists on staying.
If she can retrieve the money, she can exonerate her father.

The family try to poison the young woman at dinner, but the pollster accidentally discovers that all but one of their plates have been poisoned (the poison glows in the dark); only the dish in front of the mother's third husband, the stepfather (a third actor), is safe to eat.
The stepfather slips away, but is soon found glowing and dead.
The uneasy situation is further complicated when the real robber (a fifth actress) breaks out of prison and comes for her money.
She makes the pollster sing the song and she understands the seemingly meaningless lyrics.
The pollster gets away, and he deciphers the clues hidden in the words, from which the young woman finds a key to the safety deposit box.
Soon, all of the family, including the stepfather (who had faked his death), are chasing the pollster and the young woman through the various secret passageways of the house.
The plucky pair are able to drop each of their pursuers into a hay baling machine, from which they emerge safely.
The sheriff and his deputies then arrive rescuing the pollster and the young woman.
At his uncle's newspaper where the journalist works as a reporter specializing in chess, he is known to miss out on bigger stories to cover more trivial events of minor interest.
Confronted with an ultimatum if he wants to keep his job, the journalist is assigned to cover a big harvest festival held at a winery in the festival town.
The journalist begins with getting off the bus at the wrong stop, the nearby town instead of the festival town.
He has brought along his girlfriend the young woman, who deals in antiques.
Accidents rarely come alone, and the man sitting next to the journalist on the bus is found murdered, holding a chess piece in his hand when the police find him.
The journalist, who is a chess expert, is blamed for the killing.
All the bus passengers are held in custody at the nearby town awaiting the sheriff to start the murder investigation.
Before he arrives, the young woman finds a set of antique chess pieces she wants to acquire, and involves the journalist in her quest to buy them.
The set is said to have been the property of an ancient emperor in the 13th century, and brought to the western world by a famous explorer.
Unfortunately, the set is divided between the first twin and the second twin, twins owning the winery, who have not spoken to each other in 10 years.
The young woman manages to acquire the white set pieces from the second twin.
When the journalist is about to get the black pieces from the first twin, both he and the first twin are knocked out by an unknown attacker, who also steals the black set pieces.
The sheriff arrives, and starts conducting his investigation.
The prime suspect is convicted murderer the fugitive, who first sold the antique chess set to the twin brothers, after stealing it from its rightful owner.
The theory is that the fugitive now wants the set back to sell it back to the first owner and get the money he needs to escape the country.
The fugitive reveals himself when holding the journalist at gunpoint in his hotel room to get the white pieces from the set.
The fugitive and his accomplice the henchman hide when the young woman enters the room, telling the journalist she hid the pieces in his room.
Soon after, another guest, the other woman, also enters the room and reveals that she is an insurance agent tracking the fugitive's gang to retrieve the chess set.
She also reveals that the man killed on the bus was part of this gang of thieves.
Also at the inn is the second twin's grandson, the boy, a precocious boy genius, and his mentor, the professor.
The boy frightens the journalist with scary antics, including a pronouncement that the corpse's head was chopped off, placing a cabbage adorned by a toupee in the journalist's room.
The boy throws a smoke bomb into the room, and everyone is forced out into the corridor.
In the ensuing commotion, the white pieces are stolen.
Snooping about the winery, the journalist manages to find the black set, but is knocked unconscious in the wine cellar.
When she finds the other part of the set, the young woman is also knocked out by the boy's tutor, the professor.
The journalist wakes up, unties himself and goes after the killer, who turns out to be the professor, and ultimately finds the dead body.
After the young woman has found the complete set, the insurance adjuster the other woman offers her a $1,000 reward for retrieving it.
The journalist phones his editor, explaining the events at the nearby town and how he caught the murderer.
He then asks his editor if he should continue to the festival at the festival town or come back and get fired.
When the sleuth performs magic tricks at a Thanksgiving Day party for the inmates of a women's prison, the convict (an actress) volunteers to enter a booth.
She disappears after he draws the curtain, but as a former magician's assistant, uses the opportunity to escape.
The police inspector (an actor) takes the sleuth into custody as an accomplice, but the sleuth easily gets away himself.
A trip to the library reveals that the convict was sent to prison for three years for a robbery that netted $100,000 (which was never recovered) and a dead victim.
Her magician former husband, the conjurer, was acquitted.
The sleuth tracks the conjurer down, still performing magic, but now under the name of a stage alias, to warn him.
The convict shows up minutes later, having heard that the conjurer intends to marry his new assistant, the fiancée (another actress).
The convict has come to make sure she gets her half of the loot.
In a scuffle, she grazes the conjurer's right hand with a gunshot before fleeing.
The sleuth arranges to impersonate the conjurer, while the magician hides in the sleuth's absent friend's apartment.
That night, the sleuth is awoken by sounds in the conjurer's apartment.
When he investigates, a woman runs out of the unlit room.
The sleuth eventually locates the money in the conjurer's safety deposit box and takes it, still disguised as the conjurer.
Outside, the convict forces him at gunpoint to give her the envelope containing the loot, but when she opens it, it is empty.
The sleuth had taken the precaution of pocketing the money.
In the meantime, the sleuth's friend returns home from a trip early and finds the conjurer's body in the closet.
The police inspector corners and arrests the sleuth and his sidekick, "the little fellow" (a supporting.
actor), for murder.
The sleuth easily escapes from his cell.
Returning to the theatre where the conjurer performed, he finds an armed fiancée over the convict's lifeless body.
She admits she herself was after the money all along.
She makes the sleuth hand it over, before calling the police.
When the police inspector and his dimwitted assistant, the sergeant (a third actor), arrive, the sleuth tells them he recorded the fiancée's confession when he turned on the radio for some music.
When he plays it for them, the fiancée tries to run, but is caught and taken away.
The sleuth then informs the police inspector that there was no recording; he merely used ventriloquism to reenact his part of the prior conversation to fool the fiancée.
Ignoring the inspector's friendly advice to stop helping women, the sleuth goes to the rescue of a female being attacked by two men.
She is the woman, an old flame of his.
She begs him to help protect her baby from her husband the ex-convict, who has just been paroled.
When the ex-convict finds them together, he assumes that the child is the sleuth's and draws a gun.
A fight ensues during which an unseen third party shoots the ex-convict.
Acting on an anonymous tip, the inspector arrives soon after and assumes that the sleuth is responsible for the dead body.
The sleuth has his sidekick, the "little fellow", hide the baby at the apartment of the little fellow's girlfriend, the young lady.
The sleuth escapes from the dimwitted sergeant.
An investigation soon arouses his suspicions.
The woman and the partner are trying to swindle her wealthy father-in-law the old man.
The child is actually her brother the other man's.
They framed the sleuth in order to make the ex-convict disappear.
When the other man tries to renege, worried that he will not be given his son, the partner shoots him.
Disguised as the old man, the sleuth goes to see the pair.
He manages to overcome the partner only to have the inspector break in, arrest him and let the woman and the partner go free.
However, it is all a joke on the sleuth.
For once, the inspector has determined the identity of the real crooks.
When the sleuth goes downstairs, he sees the pair in handcuffs.
The accused man, an ex-convict, is wrongfully arrested for a bank robbery he did not commit.
The police have found fingerprints on the crime scene, incriminating the accused man.
The accused man claims to have been summoned to a theatrical warehouse by the other convict, an old cellmate—but the other convict has been dead for eight years.
Subsequently, the accused man is sentenced to death and awaits his execution.
The accused man's daughter the young woman asks private investigator the detective for help to prove her father's innocence.
Hearing about the suspicious circumstances, the detective immediately agrees to take the case.

With only nine days before the accused man's execution, the detective questions the accused man's landlady the older woman, struggling tenant the unmarried woman, bookkeeper the first gentleman, salesman the second gentleman, and showgirl the dancer, whose work costume was found in the warehouse near the crime scene.
As the detective comes closer to solving the mystery, two of the suspects are murdered.
The detective follows a number of clues, and thinks that the accused man's fingerprints may have been forged.
Working closely with a police technician, the detective proves his theory to be correct.
The detective returns to the warehouse and finds the equipment used to forge fingerprints.
There he finds the murderer, who tries to do away with the detective.
The detective solves the remaining mystery by identifying the true leader of the robbery gang, and the accused man is released from prison.
